hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
A lean season is not a buried season. Grief, illness, and limited capacity are real, and being honest about your limits isn't unfaithfulness. Small and faithful still counts.

Name the little that's in your hand, even if it's very little. If that's all you can do this week, it's enough. Read "A Pastoral Word to the 'One-Talent' Heart."

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 10
read.body:
Open to Chapter 10, "Steward What's in Your Hand Today." Read "What's in Your Hand?" and "A Practical Inventory: Name It, Then Use It."

Moses had a staff. The widow had a jar of oil. A boy had loaves and fish. The servant had one talent. God keeps starting with what's already there, not the bigger platform we're waiting for.

The inventory section is a simple, four-part practice. Read it with a pen, because the next screens will ask you to do it. Then come back.

pulse.heading: The pulse: today's portion
pulse.body:
Steward today's portion, not someday's platform.

God asked Moses a simple question, and the answer was ordinary: a staff. That's often how God starts with us too.

bookRef.chapter: Chapter 10: Steward What's in Your Hand Today

verses.text: The LORD said to him, “What is that in your hand?” He said, “A staff.”

prompts: If God asked me, "What is in your hand?" what would I say?

nameIt.heading: Name it: the domains
nameIt.body:
Chapter 10 walks through the domains of stewardship: time, gifts, relationships, work, money, influence, and the phone itself.

The widow almost missed her jar of oil. Andrew looked at five loaves and two fish and asked what they were for so many. Look at your life the same way, but with thankful eyes. And ask where someday-dreaming has been canceling today-obedience.

verses.text: And Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me; what have you in the house?” And she said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.” Then he said, “Go outside, borrow vessels from all your neighbors, empty vessels and not too few.
“There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are they for so many?”
Look carefully then how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, making the best use of the time, because the days are evil.

prompts: Which domain needs open hands most this week: time, gift, relationship, work, money, influence, or the phone itself?

What have I been calling "nothing"?

build.heading: Build it: the 10-minute inventory
build.body:
Here's the four-part inventory from Chapter 10. Give it ten minutes.

One, name what God has already given: time windows, skills, people, work, resources, influence. Don't inflate it. Don't erase the jar because it's only one jar. Two, thank Him for the portion. Gratitude breaks comparison. Three, pick one faithful use for this week. Just one. Four, review without guilt.

Make it concrete so it's hard to postpone: a day, a person, an action.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 10:

Inventory, on paper, for ten minutes. Choose one faithful use. Do it. Review Sunday: traded or buried?

Be a doer of the word, not a hearer only. If the day slips, set a new one within three days. The Sunday review is coming either way, and it's gentle.

help.heading: Help: let your light shine
help.body:
Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Tell them what's in your hand and how you used it.

Then think of someone who feels like they have nothing to offer. Don't argue them out of it. Tell them one specific thing you've seen God give them, and thank God for it.

In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.

pray.heading: Pray it: keep walking
pray.body:
Rest in who God is. Obey what is plain. Steward what's in your hand.

Lord, You asked Moses what was in his hand. Open my eyes to what's in mine.

Thank You for ____. It's not nothing. It's Yours.

This week I'll use it this way: ____. I'll do it heartily, for You. Keep me walking. Amen.

review.heading: Review Sunday: traded or not yet?
review.body:
On Sunday, look back honestly. Did you use what was in your hand this week? Mark it: traded, not yet, or holy wait. A lean week is not a buried week.

Guardrail from Chapter 10: stewardship isn't self-salvation. It isn't burnout. It doesn't neglect rest. And it isn't comparison. The two-talent servant heard the same "well done" as the five.

Look how far you've come. Fear unmasked, fog navigated, hand opened. One stop left.
